newsitem.title: EGYPT: EGPC/Repsol/Apache group find gas in west Egypt.
newsitem.headline: EGPC/Repsol/Apache group find gas in west Egypt.

text.p: Khalda Petroleum, a joint venture betwen state-owned Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation (EGPC), Repsol SA and Apache Corp, has found natural gas in Egypt's western desert, government newspaper said on Monday.
The discovery was in the Khalda concession, owned by the three shareholders, with Khalda Petroleum as operator, an oil industry source told Reuters.
Natural gas and condensates were found in three strata with a total thickness of 50 metres (160 feet), the newspapers said.
An exploratory well produced 89 million cubic feet (2.52 million cubic metres) per day of gas and 4,056 barrels per day of condensates, they added.
It is 65 km (40 miles) southwest of the Mediterranean city of Matrouh.
"The full depth of the well, South of Tut no. 1, is 13,500 feet," the source added.
He declined to say how deep the gas strata were, saying: "It (the depth of the layers) is important for competing oil firms in nearby areas as they can start exploring at the same depth."
The nearest discoveries are in the old producing area of Tut, the source said. "Khalda has made many discoveries in the concession," he added.
